title: Verifier-Guided Repair of LLM-Generated Vendor CLI Configurations: A Controlled Fault-Injection Paired Study
abstract: We evaluate whether deterministic verifier diagnostics exposed to an LLM repair workflow reduce residual unsafe or invalid vendor-CLI configurations compared with blind repair. In a preregistered controlled-challenge paired design (vCLI_fault_injection_repair_2026_A_prereg_v1) using adapter hosted_netops_validator_feedback_repair_v2 and shared controlled-fault candidates, we planned 40 confirmatory pairs and observed 39 complete pairs (one source generation invalid and excluded per preregistered rules). Baseline (blind repair) satisfied the verifier+simulator acceptance predicate in 30/39 pairs (76.92%); guarded (verifier-guided) satisfied it in 38/39 pairs (97.44%). Paired counts: n11 = 29, n10 = 9 (guarded-only), n01 = 1 (baseline-only), n00 = 0. The paired absolute difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.20512820512820507 (20.51 percentage points); two-sided exact paired test p = 0.021484375; 95% paired-bootstrap percentile CI = [0.07692307692307693, 0.358974358974359] (bootstrap resamples = 10000, seed = 1729). Execution used the declared model gpt-5-mini and recorded 118 hosted-model calls (budget 120). A preregistered confirmatory harmful-overrepair aggregation was not produced in the archived confirmatory summary; the preregistered harmful-change mapping and per-episode traces required to compute it are archived and we provide the exact artifact locations for deterministic reproduction in Methods.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed as aides in network operations (NetOps) for tasks such as intent-to-configuration translation and automated remediation. A prevalent safety-oriented architecture interposes a deterministic verifier between probabilistic generation and acceptance and, when violations are found, exposes deterministic diagnostics to a repair model (generate–verify–repair, GVR). Prior empirical work in code and Infrastructure-as-Code (IaC) settings reports that inserting deterministic verifiers into generation–repair loops can raise verifier-detected pass rates while also exposing new failure modes and operational costs [1], [2], [3], [4]. Field and survey studies of LLMs in NetOps/AIOps contexts emphasize that read-oriented assistance does not straightforwardly imply safe closed-loop autonomous changes [5].

Motivation and question. Controlled paired evidence that directly measures the causal effect of exposing deterministic verifier diagnostics to an LLM repair workflow on vendor-CLI templates with realistic preregistered fault operators is sparse. To ensure the intervention is meaningfully exercised we ran a preregistered controlled-fault injection (deterministic, outcome-independent) and a paired design that shares the same controlled-fault candidate across arms. Research question: When confronted with preregistered controlled faults across vendor-CLI templates, does exposing deterministic verifier diagnostics to an LLM repair workflow reduce residual unsafe or invalid configurations compared with blind repair?
sections.related_work:
Work on generate–verify–repair spans program repair, IaC, and DSL/code synthesis. Controlled empirical evaluations show that deterministic verifier diagnostics can materially increase verifier-detected pass rates and that supplying diagnostics to repair models improves the chance a corrected artifact satisfies the verifier on recheck [1], [2]. Separate empirical analyses demonstrate exploitation risks in iterative-refinement loops where optimization toward a single verifier proxy can degrade the underlying target property; mitigations have been proposed [3]. Other studies quantify the practical interaction and compute overheads that verifiers impose on agentic pipelines (the ‘‘verifier tax’’) and argue that such costs affect operational feasibility [4]. Survey and field case studies in NetOps/AIOps caution that apparent usefulness for read-oriented tasks does not guarantee safe closed-loop automation absent strong verification and conservative orchestration [5].

We verified that the cited records above support these adjacent claims: [1], [2], and [4] provide empirical GVR pipeline evidence and instrumentation; [3] documents verifier-exploitation cautions in controlled analyses; and [5] supplies NetOps/AIOps survey and field evidence. Each numbered citation in this paragraph was checked against the archived bibliographic records listed in References to ensure the nearby claim is supported by the primary source.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. The study was preregistered (vCLI_fault_injection_repair_2026_A_prereg_v1). Primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline, where a binary success requires both the deterministic vendor-CLI validator and a simulator-based compliance agreement. The preregistration SHA-256 is recorded in the execution manifest (preregistration_sha256 = 0ba66573928647f008b2cd5b9dde6708a61ae86ece55b693ace534e01e2b132c).

Adapter and pairing semantics. Confirmatory execution used adapter hosted_netops_validator_feedback_repair_v2 under shared_controlled_fault_candidate semantics: for each preregistered task index a single deterministically injected controlled-fault candidate (deterministic_netops_fault_injector_v1) was produced and reused unchanged across both conditions. Each pair received exactly one initial generation (shared) and exactly one repair opportunity per condition; baseline denotes blind repair (no verifier diagnostics exposed) and guarded denotes repair with deterministic validator diagnostics exposed. The archived model configuration records declared_model_version = gpt-5-mini and temperature = null (unset); null/unset does not constitute evidence of deterministic sampling and does not imply temperature = 0.

Controlled-challenge sampling and informativeness. To ensure the intervention could be meaningfully exercised we preregistered 40 deterministic controlled faults (task indices 1..40) that inject actionable violations (examples: dropped_required_restore, protected_interface_change, make_before_break switchover). The execution manifest records controlled_fault_assignment_sha256 = 8d0879872348ae94a45f3d674df57d6552624cd841b62ab239a280347f5275c6 and source_generation_attempt_count = 40 (source_valid_count = 39; source_invalid_or_failed_count = 1). The preregistered missingness rule 'complete_pair_primary' excludes a pair only if both condition executions are unscorable; one pair was excluded under this rule (both_missing_pairs = 1) and is documented in analysis/missingness_summary.csv.

Scoring, harmful-change mapping, and reproducibility. The primary success predicate required agreement of a deterministic vendor-CLI validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) and a simulator-based compliance check. The preregistration froze a harmful-change labeling schema used for the prespecified harmful-overrepair confirmatory hypothesis; the executable mapping is archived in execution/transformation_manifest.json. Compact operational rule (reproduced here): label an episode harmful if validation_after.violation_codes contains PROTECTED_INTERFACE_CHANGE or UNINTENDED_STATE_CHANGE. The per-episode validator traces include violation codes (validator_trace.violation_codes) and are archived in execution/scoring/*.json and execution/raw_results.jsonl; the transformation artifact implementing the mapping is archived at execution/transformation_manifest.json and is referenced in the full artifact manifest.

Archival pointer for runtime sampling records (required revision). Per-call runtime sampling parameters and sampling records are archived in the evidence bundle at execution/provider_calls/ and execution/raw_results.jsonl; the declared model configuration is at execution/model_configuration.json. Note that execution/model_configuration.json records temperature = null (unset); null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling and does not imply temperature = 0. Auditors can verify per-call sampling fields in execution/provider_calls/* provider-trace artifacts together with execution/raw_results.jsonl.

Statistical plan. The preregistered primary test is an exact paired binary test (two-sided McNemar exact or equivalent exact paired binomial) on the combined verifier+simulator success indicator. The analysis reports discordant-pair counts, absolute paired risk difference, two-sided exact p-value, and a 95% paired-bootstrap percentile CI (bootstrap resamples = 10000, seed = 1729). Missingness sensitivity analyses were preregistered: (1) primary excludes incomplete pairs (complete_pair_primary); (2) sensitivity treats missing episodes as failures. All raw per-episode artifacts and scoring traces required to reproduce results are archived (execution/raw_results.jsonl; execution/scoring/*.json).
sections.results:
Execution accounting and primary confirmatory outcomes. Planned confirmatory pairs = 40; completed episodes = 78 (39 complete pairs) with failed_episode_count = 2. Hosted-model calls used = 118 (≤ planned maximum 120). Source-generation attempts = 40 (source_valid_count = 39; source_invalid_or_failed_count = 1). Run timestamps and manifest pointers are recorded in the execution manifest (started_at_utc and completed_at_utc) and in the archive paths listed above.

Primary confirmatory outcomes (complete_pairs = 39). Baseline (blind repair) success = 30/39 = 0.7692307692307693. Guarded (verifier-guided) success = 38/39 = 0.9743589743589743. Paired contingency counts (guarded, baseline): n11 = 29, n10 = 9 (guarded-only), n01 = 1 (baseline-only), n00 = 0. Paired absolute difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.20512820512820507 (20.51 percentage points). Exact two-sided paired test (McNemar exact): p = 0.021484375. 95% paired-bootstrap percentile CI = [0.07692307692307693, 0.358974358974359] (bootstrap_resamples = 10000, bootstrap_seed = 1729). The archived analysis CSVs analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv and analysis/condition_summary.csv contain the numeric tables and are recorded in the artifact manifest.

Missingness and exclusions. One pair was excluded by the preregistered 'complete_pair_primary' rule because the shared source-generation was invalid/unscorable (both_missing_pairs = 1). All terminal error reasons and raw per-episode traces are archived in execution/execution_log.jsonl and execution/raw_results.jsonl for auditors.

Preregistered harmful-overrepair aggregation: status and reproducibility path. The preregistered confirmatory harmful-overrepair hypothesis (guarded does not increase harmful over-repair beyond a prespecified threshold) relied on the harmful-change mapping described in Methods. The archived confirmatory analysis executor did not compute that preregistered harmful-overrepair aggregation (secondary_results = []). Because the preregistered aggregation is absent from the archived confirmatory summary, we do not present a retroactive confirmatory safety verdict here. We provide the exact reproducibility steps and artifact locations so independent auditors can deterministically reconstruct the preregistered statistic: iterate the 39 complete pairs (analysis/missingness_summary.csv), read validation_after.violation_codes from execution/scoring/<episode>.json (or execution/raw_results.jsonl), apply the compact harmful-change rule (PROTECTED_INTERFACE_CHANGE or UNINTENDED_STATE_CHANGE → harmful), then compute paired counts and the paired difference per the analysis plan. All required per-episode fields and the transformation manifest are archived.
sections.discussion:
Interpretation and mechanism. The confirmatory paired result demonstrates a substantial increase in verifier+simulator-validated success when deterministic verifier diagnostics are exposed to the repair model under shared controlled-fault pairing semantics. The shared-candidate paired design ensures the contrast isolates the effect of exposing diagnostics because both arms received the same initial controlled-fault candidate and identical repair budgets. Per-episode validator traces in execution/scoring/*.json illustrate plausible repair pathways: diagnostics often identify specific protected fields or unintended-state changes that guarded repairs correct while blind repairs sometimes omit.

Safety boundary and unresolved preregistered safety aggregation. The preregistered harmful-overrepair confirmatory aggregation remains unresolved in the archived confirmatory summary. The preregistered harmful-change labeling rule and the per-episode traces necessary for deterministic recomputation are archived (execution/transformation_manifest.json and execution/raw_results.jsonl). We therefore preserve preregistered auditability while withholding a confirmatory safety verdict until an archived recomputation following the preregistered pipeline is incorporated into the archive.

Operational implications and verifier tax. The verifier-guided workflow materially improves verifier-defined correctness on the tested controlled faults but requires additional model–verifier interactions: the execution manifest records hosted_model_call_event_count = 118 and stage_counts (valid_source_generation = 40; blind_controlled_fault_repair = 39; validator_guided_controlled_fault_repair = 39). These counts permit exploratory computation of model-call cost per avoided failure from the archived provider traces. Verifier coverage and fidelity remain critical: a verifier that fails to detect a critical class cannot improve what it cannot see, and narrow verifier surfaces can encourage overfitting to detectable violations.

Threats to validity. Internal validity: model sampling nondeterminism (temperature = null/unset) and the exactly-one initial sampled generation per pair limit claims about deterministic generation effects; the paired contrast isolates diagnostic exposure under the adapter contract. Construct validity: primary success depends on the deterministic verifier–simulator agreement; prover/simulator mismatches constrain the operational meaning of "valid." External validity: a single declared model (gpt-5-mini) and a synthetic template-based controlled-fault bank limit generalization. Conclusion validity: with complete_pairs = 39 the primary contrast estimate has reasonable effect-size precision, but subgroup/per-fault-class inference is underpowered and exploratory.
sections.conclusion:
In a preregistered controlled-challenge paired experiment using hosted_netops_validator_feedback_repair_v2 and shared controlled-fault candidates, exposing deterministic verifier diagnostics to an LLM repair workflow produced a statistically detectable and substantial increase in verifier+simulator-validated configuration success (approx. +20.51 percentage points; p = 0.021484375; 95% CI [0.07692307692307693, 0.358974358974359]). This finding is bounded to the preregistered synthetic task bank, the declared model (gpt-5-mini), and the archived deterministic verifier and simulator. The preregistered confirmatory harmful-overrepair aggregation was not produced in the archived confirmatory summary and therefore remains unresolved for the confirmatory claim; the archived artifacts and transformation manifest provide exact inputs and a deterministic recomputation path so auditors can reproduce that preregistered statistic. We release the artifact bundle for reproducible reaggregation and recommend multi-model, multi-verifier replications and larger-scale cost/latency studies to assess operational feasibility and safety at NetOps scale.

References
[1] R. Cadenas, "Convergent Correctness in Stochastic Code Generation: A Generate–Verify–Repair Architecture for Deterministic Validation of Autonomous AI Coding Agents in Regulated Environments," SSRN, 2026. doi: 10.2139/ssrn.6754899.
[2] M. Jouini, "Verifier-First Evaluation of Agentic LLMs for Infrastructure-as-Code Generation," arXiv preprint arXiv:2607.20478, 2026.
[3] A. Gupta, "Verifier Exploitation in NLI-Guided Iterative Refinement: A Controlled Empirical Analysis," Research Square, 2026. doi: 10.21203/rs.3.rs-10187492/v1.
[4] T. Sah et al., "The Verifier Tax: Horizon Dependent Safety Success Tradeoffs in Tool Using LLM Agents," arXiv preprint arXiv:2603.19328, 2026.
[5] M. Bilal, J. Crowcroft, R. Wang, X. Xu, and S. Dustdar, "Large Language Models for Agentic NetOps and AIOps: Architectures, Evaluation, and Safety," arXiv preprint arXiv:2605.12729, 2026.

disclosure_statement: Preregistration: vCLI_fault_injection_repair_2026_A_prereg_v1 (preregistration_sha256 recorded in execution manifest). Adapter: hosted_netops_validator_feedback_repair_v2. Declared model used for confirmatory execution: gpt-5-mini (declared_model_version recorded in execution/model_configuration.json). Exact initial master prompt archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA-256: f781dd7978328198146d586cf33e0f4b783c8db126bd0f16fcd13699455ebb10) and cited here by immutable archive reference. Human role: a Research Director selected the topic family and pre-lock constraints; after the autonomy lock the autonomous system performed literature verification, preregistration, experiment execution, analysis, and manuscript generation; no manual human editing of technical manuscript content occurred after the lock. Execution semantics: execution manifest records temperature = null/unset in execution/model_configuration.json; null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling and does not imply temperature = 0. Pairing semantics: exactly one sampled initial generation per task pair was performed and reused by both arms under shared_controlled_fault_candidate semantics; baseline denotes blind repair (no validator diagnostics exposed) and guarded denotes repair with deterministic validator diagnostics exposed. Harmful-change mapping and reconstructability: the preregistered harmful-change rules were frozen and the transformation artifact implementing the mapping is archived (see execution/transformation_manifest.json and the full artifact manifest execution/execution_manifest.json in the evidence bundle). Per-episode raw traces and scoring artifacts required to reproduce all aggregated confirmatory and preregistered secondary statistics are archived (execution/raw_results.jsonl; execution/scoring/*.json; analysis/*.csv). The study followed the preregistered stopping rule; no silent adapter substitution occurred.
limitations: Synthetic controlled-fault task bank: tasks were deterministically injected and do not represent a broad naturalistic distribution of production NetOps incidents; external validity to live operator workloads is limited.
Single-model and single-adapter evaluation: confirmatory execution used only the declared model gpt-5-mini and one adapter family; results do not establish multi-model generality.
Simulator-backed primary success predicate: primary success required agreement of deterministic verifier and simulator; simulator fidelity and verifier coverage constrain construct validity.

Sample size and power: complete_pairs = 39 provides detectable effects of the observed magnitude but limits precision for subgroup and per-fault-class inference; exploratory subgroup analyses are not confirmatory.
Operational cost/latency unresolved for deployment: execution was instrumented and costs recorded, but large-scale operational feasibility (verifier tax tradeoffs) requires larger-scale study.

Verifier-exploitation and long-horizon agentic pathologies remain possible: this controlled setting mitigates some risks, but broader agentic workflows need additional defenses (multi-verifier designs, calibrated abstention, uncertainty quantification).

Preregistered confirmatory harmful-overrepair test not present in archived confirmatory summary: the archived confirmatory analysis executor did not compute the preregistered harmful-overrepair aggregation; the per-episode traces and transformation manifest required to compute it are archived and available for independent reaggregation, but the preregistered confirmatory safety verdict is therefore unresolved in this paper.
